narrative.overview: Conductor is where Converted Click runs its business, and it should feel like the agency's own studio surface — human, considered, a little crafted — not generic internal software. Built on Material 3 role tokens (violet primary, Inter type, a tonal surface ramp) synced from Figma. Warmth lives in copy, empty states, and feedback; precision lives in the numbers, tables, and money-bearing flows. The signature violet→pink brand gradient is held in reserve for primary actions and identity moments, never sprayed as decoration. A product register for expert operators: density and speed over onboarding theatre, but always legible and unhurried. Components are soft and approachable — full-round pills, generous padding, gently lifted cards.
keyCharacteristics: Violet-forward Material 3 palette with a violet→pink gradient reserved for primary actions
Inter as the single UI family; JetBrains Mono for figures and code
Fixed rem type scale (not fluid) — product density, consistent DPI
Soft, full-round controls and gently lifted cards; warm, not clinical
Light and dark modes, both first-class; WCAG AA baseline

rules.name: The Reserved Gradient Rule
rules.body: The violet→pink bg-gradient-brand appears only on primary actions and identity moments — never a section background, hero wash, or decoration. Its scarcity keeps it from reading as the AI-SaaS cliché.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Gray Rule
rules.body: Body text is Ink (#09090B), never a light elegance-gray. Secondary text is violet-tinted Muted Ink and still clears 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Currency, hours, percentages, and IDs render in JetBrains Mono so figures tabulate and read as exact.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: The type scale is fixed rem, never fluid clamp(). Product density depends on consistent sizing across every panel.

rules.name: The Soft-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are slate-tinted and low-opacity, layered subtly — never a hard 2014-era drop shadow.

dos: Do reserve the violet→pink bg-gradient-brand for primary actions and identity moments only.
Do set body text in Ink (#09090B) and keep secondary text at violet-tinted Muted Ink that clears 4.5:1.
Do use full-round pills for buttons and rounded-lg cards with a soft elev-1 resting shadow.
Do render currency, hours, and IDs in JetBrains Mono so figures tabulate.
Do bring hierarchy to dense data — group, summarize, right-align numbers — instead of raw grids.
Do use the m- / shadcn token classes, never hardcoded hex; tokens are Figma-synced and generated.
Do provide every interactive state and teach-the-interface empty states.
donts: Don't recreate enterprise/SAP heaviness — gray, joyless, form-on-every-screen legacy admin.
Don't ship the generic AI-SaaS template: no purple-gradient hero wash, identical card grids, tracked eyebrows, or big-number-metric cliché.
Don't allow spreadsheet sprawl — raw hierarchy-less grids are the mess Conductor replaces.
Don't use light elegance-gray for body text, or faint placeholders below 4.5:1.
Don't hand-edit src/styles/tokens.css or tokens.ts — they're generated from tokens/base.json.
Don't use fluid clamp() heading scales, hard/dark drop shadows, side-stripe borders, gradient text, or default glassmorphism.
Don't nest cards, or reach for a modal before exhausting inline/progressive alternatives.
